Reading in some tools!


```{r}
#| warnings: hold
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
```
### Reading Data and EDA

This dataset keeps track of rented bikes / hour in Seoul, as well as a collection of climate and business metrics.

By default, make.names() replaces weird characters (degrees, ^2, etc.)
with periods, so the second line just removes those periods.
```{r}
bike <- read_csv("https://www4.stat.ncsu.edu/~online/datasets/SeoulBikeData.csv", 
                 locale = locale(encoding = "latin1"))

## By default, make.names() replaces weird characters (degrees, ^2, etc.)
## with periods, so this line just removes those periods
colnames(bike) <- gsub("\\.", "", make.names(colnames(bike)))

bike <- bike|>
  mutate(
    Date = dmy(Date),
    Seasons = as.factor(Seasons),
    Holiday = as.factor(Holiday),
    FunctioningDay = as.factor(FunctioningDay)
  )
```
```{r}
summary(bike)
bike |>
  summarize(across(everything(), ~sum(is.na(.)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything())
```
No `N/A` values? How nice :) And no values of -200 or anything like that either.

Create summary statistics of numerical variables across categorical variables.

```{r}
mysummary <- function(data, variable){
  summary <- data |>
    group_by(get(variable)) |>
    summarize(n = n(),
              across(where(is.numeric),
                     list("mean" = mean, "median" = median, "sd" = sd, "IQR" = IQR),
                     .names = "{.fn}_{.col}"))
  colnames(summary)[1] <- variable
  return(summary)
}

mysummary(bike, "Seasons")
mysummary(bike, "Holiday")
mysummary(bike, "FunctioningDay")
```

When `FunctioningDay` is "No", `RentedBikeCount` is 0. Based on that, we will subset the data to exclude the non-functioning days.

```{r}
#filter to functioning days
bike <- bike |>
  filter(FunctioningDay == "Yes")

#re-run the numerical summaries
mysummary(bike, "Seasons")
mysummary(bike, "Holiday")
mysummary(bike, "FunctioningDay")
```

Based on the summaries, it looks like our data is pretty evenly spread throughout the year - ~2000 measurements a season.

Grouping the data by date - Step 7
```{r}
bike_daily <- bike |>
  group_by(Date, Seasons, Holiday)|>
  summarize(across(c(RentedBikeCount, Rainfallmm, Snowfallcm), sum),
            across(c(TemperatureC:SolarRadiationMJm2), mean))          
```

Recreate basic summary stats.

```{r}
summary(bike_daily)
mysummary(bike_daily, "Seasons")
mysummary(bike_daily, "Holiday")
```

create some plots to explore relationships.

The plot below looks at bike rental counts and temperatures across dates.

```{r}
ggplot(bike_daily, aes(x = Date, y = RentedBikeCount, color = TemperatureC))+
  geom_point()+
  labs(title = "Rentals by date")
```

The plots below look at bike rental counts across seasons and whether it is a holiday.

```{r}
ggplot(bike_daily, aes(x = Seasons, y = RentedBikeCount, fill = Holiday)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "Rentals by Season")

ggplot(bike_daily, aes(x = Seasons, y = RentedBikeCount, fill = Holiday)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Rentals by Season")
```

The plot below looks at the relationship between bike rentals and rainfall.

```{r}
ggplot(bike_daily, aes(x = Rainfallmm, y = RentedBikeCount, color = Seasons)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = lm) +
  labs(title = "Rentals by Rainfall")
```

All of the above plots support the idea that bike rentals are higher during the warmer seasons. Bike rentals also seem to be lower on holidays and lower when it is raining.

We can quantify some of these patterns further by reporting correlation statistics.

```{r}
bike_daily |>
  group_by(c()) |>
  summarize(across(where(is.numeric),
                   list("correlation" = ~ cor(.x, RentedBikeCount)),
            .names = "cor_{.col}")) |>
  pivot_longer(starts_with("cor_"))
```

### Split the Data

Split the data into a training and testing set (75/25 split), stratified by Seasons.

```{r}
set.seed(10)
bike_split <- rsample::initial_split(bike_daily, prop = 0.75, strata = Seasons)
training <- training(bike_split)
testing <- testing(bike_split)

#view training set
training

#view testing set
testing
```

### Fitting MLR Models

Create Weekday/Weekend (factor) variable and standardize numeric variables.
```{r}
# Create a function to output weekday or weekend as a factor variable
date_factor <- function(Date) {
  wend_wday <- wday(Date,
       label = TRUE)
  weekend <- ifelse(wend_wday %in% c("Sat", "Sun"), "Weekend", "Weekday")
  return(as.factor(weekend))
}

# Modify training data set
training <- training |>
  mutate(Weekend = date_factor(Date))

# View training data set
training

# Modify testing data set |>
testing <- testing |>
  mutate(Weekend = date_factor(Date))

# View testing data set
testing

# Standardized numeric variables for the test and training sets

std_training <- training |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    across(where(is.numeric) & !all_of("RentedBikeCount"),
      ~ (.x - mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)) /
        sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )

train_means <- training |>
  ungroup() |> 
  summarise(
    across(where(is.numeric) & !all_of("RentedBikeCount"),
      ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )

train_sds <- training |>
  ungroup() |> 
  summarise(
    across(where(is.numeric) & !all_of("RentedBikeCount"),
      ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )

std_testing <- testing |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    across(where(is.numeric) & !all_of("RentedBikeCount"),
      ~ (.x - train_means[[cur_column()]]) /
          train_sds[[cur_column()]]
    )
  )

```



#### Fitting Models
First model is to use the Rented Bike Count as our target variable and all other variables as our features.  Use RMSE as the metric to evaluate the fit of the model using the training data.

```{r}
#fit model with all variables
names(std_training)
all_var_fit <- lm(RentedBikeCount ~ .-Date, std_training)

summary(all_var_fit)
#predict the y values for the x values in the test set
Y_test <- predict(all_var_fit, newdata = std_testing)

#Calculate the RMSE for the test set
rmse_var <- rmse_vec(
  truth = std_testing$RentedBikeCount,
  estimate = Y_test)
```
Second model is to use Rented Bike Count as our target variable and all the terms in the first model but also interactions between seasons and holiday, seasons and temp, and temp and rainfall (all standardized variables used here).
```{r}
names(std_training)
#fit the model with all the variables and the interaction terms
interaction_var_fit <- lm(RentedBikeCount ~ . -Date +Seasons:Holiday +Seasons:TemperatureC+TemperatureC:Rainfallmm, std_training)

#See the results of the model
summary(interaction_var_fit)

#predict the y values for the x values in the test set
Y_test_inter <- predict(interaction_var_fit, newdata = std_testing)

#Calculate the RMSE for the test set
rmse_inter <- rmse_vec(
  truth = std_testing$RentedBikeCount,
  estimate = Y_test_inter)
```
Third model is to use Rented Bike Count as our target variable and all the terms in the first model plus the interaction terms in the second model and include quadratic terms of temperature and humidity squared (all standardized variables used here).
```{r}
#fit the model with all the variables, the interaction terms, and the quadratic terms
quad_var_fit <- lm(RentedBikeCount ~ . -Date +Seasons:Holiday +Seasons:TemperatureC+TemperatureC:Rainfallmm + I(TemperatureC^2) +I(Humidity^2), data = std_training)

#See the results of the model
summary(quad_var_fit)

#predict the y values for the x values in the test set
Y_test_quad <- predict(quad_var_fit, newdata=std_testing)


#Calculate the RMSE for the test set
rmse_quad <- rmse_vec(
  truth = std_testing$RentedBikeCount,
  estimate = Y_test_quad)

c(Main_Effects = rmse_var,
  Interactions = rmse_inter,
  Quadratic = rmse_quad)

```


Model 1: The RMSE for all variables is 3530.921

Model 2: The RMSE for all variables plus the interaction terms is 3128.248

Model 3: The RMSE for all variables, interaction terms, and quadratic terms is 3133.055

The model that minimizes the test set RMSE is Model 2 which includes all the variables and the interaction terms. 

Fit that model to the entire data set to create the final fitted model.

```{r}
#Standardize the variables with all the data
std_bike_daily <- bike_daily |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    across(where(is.numeric) & !all_of("RentedBikeCount"),
      ~ (.x - mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)) /
        sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )


#fit the model with all the variables and the interaction terms and all data
interaction_var_fit_full <- lm(RentedBikeCount ~ . -Date +Seasons:Holiday +Seasons:TemperatureC+TemperatureC:Rainfallmm, std_bike_daily)

#See the results of the model
summary(interaction_var_fit_full)

#predict the y values for the x values in the test set
Y_test_inter_full <- predict(interaction_var_fit_full, newdata = std_bike_daily)

#Calculate the RMSE for the test set
rmse_inter_full <- rmse_vec(
  truth = std_bike_daily$RentedBikeCount,
  estimate = Y_test_inter_full)
rmse_inter

#Report the coefficients of the final fitted model
coefficients_full <- data.frame(
  Term = names(coef(interaction_var_fit_full)),
  Coefficient = coef(interaction_var_fit_full)
)

coefficients_full
```
